key_insight: Variable-geometry sample-based quantum diagonalization (VGSQD) reuses quantum samples across molecular geometries, reducing quantum computational cost for geometry optimization and reaction-path calculations.
engineering_relevance: The method extends quantum chemistry workflows beyond fixed-geometry energies toward molecular structures and reaction barriers relevant to catalysis and molecular design.
method: Generate quantum samples at a reference molecular geometry.
Reuse those samples for subspace diagonalization at displaced geometries.
Use the resulting energies to optimize structures and map reaction pathways.
evidence_signal: Using circuits of up to 124 qubits on IBM's ibm-quebec Heron r2 processor, the authors evaluated beryllium dimer and water equilibrium geometries and energies, plus a hydrogen-exchange reaction pathway and barrier, reporting results comparable to CCSD(T) and DMRG.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify cost savings or establish how far samples can be reused as molecular geometry changes.
paper_title: Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization for Variable Molecular Geometries
